WMT.rationale: Walmart is a high-quality franchise with genuine structural growth optionality through its advertising, membership, and marketplace services layer. Operating margin has expanded 100bps over three years to 4.6%, ROIC improved from 5% to 18%, and global ad revenue grew 46% to $6.4B. However, the stock is priced for near-flawless execution at 53.8x trailing PE (62% expansion in 12 months vs only 35% EPS growth), 1.9% earnings yield vs 4.41% risk-free (-251bps negative spread), and 11.6x P/B. QoQ operating margin compressed from 4.11% to 3.73%, QoQ EPS declined 12.5%, and oil at $98/bbl introduces cost headwinds not yet in margins. Grocery share is eroding (20.4% to 19.9%), tariff timing is pressuring Q1, and pharmacy pricing regulation creates a ~100bps revenue headwind. The market has absorbed the positive trajectory and then some — the 62% PE expansion far exceeds the 35% earnings growth rate. At this valuation, any slowdown in the services mix-shift or margin expansion gets penalized hard. The business is materially more attractive than the stock.
key_factors: PE diluted 53.8x as of 2026-05-07, up 62% from 33.2x twelve months ago — far exceeding 35% YoY EPS growth of $0.77 vs $0.57
Earnings yield 1.9% sits -251bps below 10Y treasury at 4.41%, implying aggressive expectations for sustained acceleration from a 2.8% net margin retailer
QoQ operating margin compressed to 3.73% (Q3) from 4.11% (Q2); QoQ EPS declined -12.5% to $0.77 from $0.88; QoQ net income fell -14.9%
WTI crude at $98.38/bbl (+52.5% from Feb) pressures logistics costs for a distribution-heavy retailer; not yet reflected in margin trajectory
Grocery market share eroding from 20.4% (2024) to 19.9% (2026) per Numerator data, contradicting unassailable dominance narrative
Tariff timing pre-guided lower Q1 operating income; Maximum Fair Pricing legislation expected to create ~100bps revenue headwind for FY2027
Global advertising revenue grew 46% to $6.4B and ROIC improved from 5% to 18% — genuine structural quality, but already capitalized at 53.8x PE
UBS $147 target and mid-6% operating margin by 2030 projection requires aggressive sustained execution; Henry Fund DCF produces intrinsic value of only $83.24

sources_cited.excerpt: operating_income=7.29B, eps_diluted=0.88 (QoQ margin compression from Q2 to Q3)
Walmart's leading share of the grocery market continues to decline, according to the latest data from Numerator. Walmart currently holds a 19.9% share, down from 20% in 2025 and 20.4% in 2024

At 43x forward earnings, Walmart isn't being valued on what it earns today. It's being valued on a future where advertising and membership keep expanding their share of profits. Any slowdown in that shift, or gross margin pressure from tariffs on general merchandise, gets penalized hard at this multiple

Operating Margins: A standout metric for 2026, margins expanded to 4.6% in the final quarter. This 100-basis-point improvement over the last three years is attributed to the 'mixing up' of the business toward high-margin advertising and membership fees
Walmart's ROIC has improved dramatically over the past five years, rising from 5% in fiscal 2021 to 18% in fiscal 2026

Walmart's global advertising revenue grew 46% in fiscal 2026 to nearly $6.4 billion... Lasser projects that Walmart's enterprise-wide EBIT could rise from approximately $29.5 billion in 2025 to roughly $53.7 billion by 2030

Management has already pre-guided for lower Q1 operating income growth due to tariff timing, and Maximum Fair Pricing legislation on pharmacy is expected to create a 100 basis point revenue headwind for the full fiscal year
Henry Fund DCF produces an intrinsic value of $83.24
